question: The S.I unit of induced-potential difference is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **S.I unit of induced-potential difference** is **Volt (V)**.
 
• The volt is the derived unit for electric potential, electric potential difference (voltage), and electromotive force.
 
• It is named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta.
 
• **1 Volt** is defined as the potential difference across a conductor **when a current of 1 ampere dissipates 1 watt of power.**
 
• The symbol for volt is **V**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of electric potential difference is essential in understanding how electric circuits work.
 
• It is a measure of the **work needed to move a charge from one point to another in an electric field**.
 
• In practical terms, it is what drives electric current through a circuit.
 
• Various instruments like voltmeters are used to measure the potential difference in circuits.
 
• Volt is a crucial unit in both theoretical and applied physics, especially in the fields of electronics and electrical engineering.
